'''Piet Gros''' (born July 31, 1962 in [[Dokkum]]) is a Dutch chemist and professor biomacromolecular crystallography at [[Utrecht University]]. In 2010 he received the [[Netherlands Organisation for Scientific Research|NWO]] [[Spinoza Prize]] for the elucidation of the three-dimensional structure of the [[Complement component 3|C3 protein]], which plays a central role in the [[complement system]] and contributes to [[innate immunity]].

== Biography ==
Gros was born in Dokkum, [[Netherlands]]. He studied chemistry at the [[University of Groningen]], where he graduated [[cum laude]] with a master's degree. Five years later Gros received his PhD degree cum laude at the same university, with a thesis on [[protein crystallography]]. Subsequently he became a postdoctoral researcher at the [[ETH Zurich]] and later at [[Yale University]]. In 1994 Gros was given a position at Utrecht University to conduct experimental research towards new applications for protein crystallography. In 2002 he was given the position of full professor. From 2007 until 2010 Gros was head of the department of chemistry and from 2012 to 2016 he was scientific director of the [[Bijvoet Centre for Biomolecular Research]].<ref name="LC">{{cite news
|title=Pionier in eiwit: Interview met Piet Gros
|author= Anko de Jong
|date=June 12, 2010
|newspaper=[[Leeuwarder Courant]]
|language=Dutch
}}</ref> Gros received an ERC Advanced grant of the [[European Research Council]] in 2008,<ref name="UU_ERC">{{cite web
|title=Utrechtse hoogleraren Piet Gros en Marco van Leeuwen krijgen ERC Advanced Grant
|language=Dutch
|website=www.uu.nl
|date=November 17, 2008
|url=http://www.uu.nl/NL/Actueel/Pages/UtrechtsehooglerarenPietGrosenMarcovanLeeuwenkrijgenERCAdvancedGrant.aspx}}</ref> is a member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (KNAW) since 2010<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/members/11061 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200224144919/https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/members/11061 |title=Piet Gros |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |date= |archive-date=February 24, 2020}}</ref> and in April 2013, Gros became Knight in the [[Order of the Netherlands Lion]], when he received a Royal Decoration for his scientific achievements.<ref name="UU_RD">{{cite web
|title=Zeven Koninklijke onderscheidingen aan de Universiteit Utrecht
|language=Dutch
|date=April 26, 2013
|website=www.uu.nl
|url=http://pers.uu.nl/koninklijke-onderscheidingen-universiteit-utrecht/
}}</ref><ref name="DUB_RD">{{cite news
|title=Lintjesregen in Academiegebouw
|date=April 26, 2013
|author=Xander Bronkhorst
|url=http://www.dub.uu.nl/artikel/nieuws/lintjesregen-academiegebouw.html
|language=Dutch
|publisher=DUB}}</ref>

== Research ==
The main expertise  of Gros is in the area of protein crystallography methodology and its application to large human plasma proteins and cell-surface receptors and membrane proteins.<ref name="UU_Pgros">{{cite web
|title=prof. dr. P. (Piet) Gros
|url=http://www.uu.nl/staff/PGros
|accessdate=May 1, 2013
|website=www.uu.nl}}</ref> Among his findings are the molecular mechanisms that underlie key steps in the human immune defense by the complement system, such as the mode of action of complement component 3<ref name="C3b_2">{{cite journal
|doi=10.1126/science.1195821
|title=Structures of C3b in Complex with Factors B and D Give Insight into Complement Convertase Formation
|year=2010
|last1=Forneris
|first1=F.
|last2=Ricklin
|first2=D.
|last3=Wu
|first3=J.
|last4=Tzekou
|first4=A.
|last5=Wallace
|first5=R. S.
|last6=Lambris
|first6=J. D.
|last7=Gros
|first7=P.
|journal=Science
|volume=330
|issue=6012
|pages=1816–20
|pmid=21205667
|pmc=3087196|bibcode=2010Sci...330.1816F
}}</ref> and [[C8 complex|component 8]].<ref name="C3b_1">{{cite journal
|doi=10.1126/science.1147103
|title=Structure of C8 -MACPF Reveals Mechanism of Membrane Attack in Complement Immune Defense
|year=2007
|last1=Hadders
|first1=M. A.
|last2=Beringer
|first2=D. X.
|last3=Gros
|first3=P.
|journal=Science
|volume=317
|issue=5844
|pages=1552–4
|pmid=17872444|hdl=1874/26831
|s2cid=44959101
|hdl-access=free
}}</ref> Other research in his lab has focussed on the adhesion of [[von Willebrand factor]] (A1 domain) to its platelet receptor GpIb and the structures of pathogenic bacterial outer-membrane proteins<ref name="UU_Pgros"/> and the movement of individual atoms within the defined protein structures.<ref name="ScienceGuide">{{cite web
|title=Beweging moleculen in beeld
|language=Dutch
|website=ScienceGuide
|accessdate=May 1, 2013
|url=http://www.scienceguide.nl/201212/beweging-moleculen-in-beeld.aspx|date=2012-12-21
}}</ref>

==Honours and awards==
In 2010, Gros received the [[Netherlands Organisation for Scientific Research|NWO]] [[Spinoza Prize]] for the elucidation of the three-dimensional structure of the [[Complement component 3|C3 protein]]. This protein is part of the oldest part of the [[immune system]] that is present in the human body, the [[complement system]]. Using [[structural biology]] techniques such as protein crystallography, the research group of Gros studies structures and chemical interactions that are at the basis of immunological processes such as the complement system.<ref name="NWO">{{cite web
 |title       = Spinozawinnaars 2010
 |date        = June 7, 2010
 |url         = http://www.nwo.nl/nwohome.nsf/pages/NWOP_5VNCW6
 |publisher   = NWO
 |url-status     = dead
 |archiveurl  = https://web.archive.org/web/20121029184200/http://www.nwo.nl/nwohome.nsf/pages/NWOP_5VNCW6
 |archivedate = October 29, 2012
}}</ref><ref name="Volkskrant">{{cite news
|newspaper=[[Volkskrant]]
|title=Winnaar Spinozapremie 2010: Piet Gros, biomacromoleculair kristallograaf
|date=June 7, 2010
|url=http://www.volkskrant.nl/vk/nl/2672/Wetenschap-Gezondheid/article/detail/996612/2010/06/07/Winnaar-Spinozapremie-2010-Piet-Gros-biomacromoleculair-kristallograaf.dhtml
|language=Dutch}}</ref><ref name="sciencenewsline">{{cite web
|website=www.sciencenewsline.com
|title=NWO Spinoza Prize for Psychologist, Astronomer, Chemist And Classicist
|date=June 7, 2010
|url=http://www.sciencenewsline.com/articles/2010060700007699.html
|access-date=May 1, 2013
|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130615193019/http://www.sciencenewsline.com/articles/2010060700007699.html
|archive-date=June 15, 2013
|url-status=dead
}}</ref> He is the recipient of the 2018 [[Gregori Aminoff Prize]], an international prize awarded since 1979 by the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences in the field of crystallography.<ref>{{Cite web|title=This year's crystallography prize awarded to a world-leading protein researcher
|url=http://www.kva.se/en/pressrum/pressmeddelanden/arets-pris-i-kristallografi-till-varldsledande-proteinforskare|date=September 15, 2017|accessdate=2017-09-19}}</ref>
In 2024, he was awarded the ICS Legacy Award of the International Complement Society <ref>{{Cite web|title=2024 Legacy Awardee - Piet Gros|url=https://www.complement.org/News/13329763|date=March 14, 2024|accessdate=2024-05-07}}</ref> and the Bijvoet Medal of the Bijvoet Centre for Biomolecular Research.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Bijvoet Medal awarded to Piet Gros|url=https://www.uu.nl/en/news/bijvoet-medal-awarded-to-piet-gros|date=May 6, 2024|accessdate=2024-05-07}}</ref>
